title: LanguageDeclaration
description: What a language declares beside its lexicon (lexicons/<lang>/language.yaml; ADR 0145, 0148): the varieties and registers a scope ranges over, the dimensions of each category, the features and values its tokens and lexemes carry, its defaults and its classes. A category is a UD tag: no category system is declared (the owner, round 6). Every statement here is content: drafted `llm:` and REVIEW until signed off.

varieties.description: The varieties a scope may name (ADR 0145), as BCP 47 tags: es-CU, es-ES, apc-LB.

registers.description: The registers a scope may name.

dimensions.description: For each category, the inflectional features every member must choose a value of (ADR 0145: what makes a head a value head). Spanish NOUN: [Number]; apc VERB: [Aspect, Person, Gender, Number].

features.description: Every feature the language's tokens and lexemes may carry, with its values: UD's names where UD has the feature (Tense: [Past, Pres]), the language's own where it has none.

defaults.description: The language's stated defaults (ADR 0148: a default is a rule; ADR 0146: what one gives is no part of a lexeme). Spanish: a noun in -a is feminine.

classes.description: The language's stated classes (ADR 0148: stated, never counted). A lexeme that belongs to one stores it, and it is a part to learn (ADR 0146).

Condition.title: Condition
Condition.description: What a default, an allomorph or (later) a rule's branch looks at in a lexeme or a base (ADR 0148: a rule's conditions). Every key given must hold. A first, small set: it grows with the rule format, which is not designed yet.

ends.description: The lexical form ends in this (Spanish -a; uz -k).

starts.description: The lexical form begins with this.

class.description: It belongs to this class of its language.

Default.title: Default
Default.description: One default: where `when` holds of a lexeme, it has `gives` unless its entry says otherwise.

notes.description: What a reviewer should know, by support language.

LexicalClass.title: LexicalClass
LexicalClass.description: One class: a lexical feature a rule reads and no form gives (Spanish e-ie; the -go verbs).

gloss.description: What a learner is shown for it, by support language (pensar: e → ie).

notes.description: What a reviewer should know, by support language.
